$comment: Size budgets for the production build, enforced by scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs (docs/SAAS.md CAP-101).

Raising a number here is allowed — it is a deliberate, reviewable decision about what staff download on ward wifi, which is exactly what a budget is for. Raising one WITHOUT first finding out what grew is how the two regressions this gate exists to catch got in.
Measured 2026-08-30. Headroom is roughly 15%: tight enough to catch a regression, loose enough that ordinary feature work does not trip it.

precacheGzipKiB.why: What a first visit downloads before the app is usable offline. The number that matters most: a carer on hospital wifi pays it once, in full, up front.

precacheEntries.why: Guards chunk-count explosions. PR #75: thirteen DEV preview pages were defined outside the import.meta.env.DEV guard, so Rollup emitted a chunk for each and Workbox precached all thirteen — 87 kB of fabricated staff names shipped to every user.

entryJsGzipKiB.why: The entry chunk blocks first paint and is the tell for code-splitting collapse. If a lazy route becomes a static import this grows while the per-route chunks vanish — the regression PR #69 fixed, where opening /app/clock pulled in the rest of the app.

shippedGzipKiB.why: Every JS and CSS file that reaches the server, service worker included. Excludes .map, which cpanel-deploy does not deploy.
